h1: How do wetlands protection laws affect home projects in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Wetlands Protection: Home Projects and Conservation Review
description: Learn which types of land work near wetlands and waterways require Conservation Commission review.
short_answer: Newton requires Conservation Commission review for land-altering work within 100 feet of a vegetated wetland, intermittent stream, or pond; within 200 feet of a perennial stream; or in a FEMA or City floodplain. The state Wetlands Protection Act also regulates alteration of protected resource areas. A permit may be required before work begins.

facts.text: Newton identifies work within 100 feet of a vegetated wetland, intermittent stream, or pond and within 200 feet of a perennial stream as requiring Conservation Commission review.
Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 131, Section 40 regulates removal, filling, dredging, or alteration of specified wetlands and other protected resource areas.

qa.q: Does wetlands review apply only when a homeowner builds directly in a wetland?
qa.a: No. Newton identifies review areas extending beyond the resource itself, including the 100-foot and 200-foot areas listed in its wetlands guidance.
